newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Suncorp says safe from bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: Suncorp says safe from bank mergers.

text.p: Queensland mega-bank Suncorp Metway Ltd said it would be safe from takeover activity following expected bank industry rationalisation in response to the Wallis financial system inquiry.

"We believe we will be on the sidelines (of any activity) for several years because of the (Queensland state) government's 67 percent stake," chief executive Steve Jones told a Morgan Stockbroking Ltd breakfast meeting.
The Wallis inquiry recommended, and the government agreed to, an end to the "six pillars" policy which prevented mergers between big banks and the nation's two largest insurance firms.
"We don't believe there'll be a major effect on us," Jones said.
The Wallis inquiry's recommendation of a single prudential supervisory body for the banking industry was a welcome move, he said.
"From our point of view, we are very pleased with one prudential supervisor," Jones said.
Moves to rationalise the new group's structure following the merger of Suncorp, Metway Bank Ltd and Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) were moving quickly, Jones said.
A total of 250 positions were targeted for removal by June 30 with the rationalisation programme expected to be completed in about 18 months, he said.
Jones declined to estimate job loss numbers from the current 5,000 staff.
"But we would hope to have the bulk finished by the end of the next financial year," he said.
